03 / FEATURED CASE STUDY

Face Recognition for Intelligent Library Management

A web-based library system that uses facial recognition to identify users and support book borrowing and returns without requiring a physical ID card.

My role
Programmer
Built for
ISAT-U Miagao Campus Library
Team
Four students and one adviser
Project stack
Python, OpenCV, PHP, HTML, MySQL, AJAX
Method
Modified Waterfall Model
Evaluation
ISO/IEC 25010:2023

The problem

At ISAT-U Miagao, library transactions relied on physical ID cards and manual record-keeping. Lost cards, verification delays, and human error could slow service. Staff also had to track borrowed and overdue books and calculate fines manually.

The solution

The system uses facial recognition to identify registered users, supports book borrowing and returns, and calculates overdue fines. It also brings user profiles, book records, and transaction histories together in one central database.

What it does

  • Registers students, faculty members, and staff
  • Supports book borrowing and returns through facial recognition
  • Tracks borrowed books
  • Calculates fines for overdue books
  • Generates reports on borrowing history, fines, and user records

How the pieces connect

  1. Library userA student, faculty member, or staff member
  2. CameraCaptures the user’s facial image
  3. ComputerProcesses the image and runs the recognition system
  4. DatabaseStores and retrieves library records
Administrator manages user records, book information, and fines using the computer.

This is a simplified explanation of the system architecture shown in our capstone manuscript. The system calculated fines but did not process payments; payments continued to follow the library’s existing procedures.

Technology

The facial-recognition component was developed using Python and OpenCV. HTML and PHP powered the user interface and server-side functions, while MySQL stored the system records. The project was evaluated using ISO/IEC 25010:2023. IT experts rated the system Excellent overall, while end users rated it Very Satisfactory.

  • Python
  • OpenCV
  • PHP
  • HTML
  • MySQL
  • AJAX

My role and how we worked

I served as the team’s programmer, working primarily with PHP, MySQL, and AJAX. During my library internship, I also assisted students with borrowing and returning books using the completed system.

Our four-student team followed a modified waterfall approach, working through sequential development phases and using feedback to make revisions. We were guided by our adviser, Jason Mendoza. Vanneza led the team, John Loyd served as the analyst, and Nhorexel served as the documenter.
